comment: Compiled to per-material GPU buckets at load (hot-reload with R). chance is per-mille per 30 Hz tick. Rules for the same self are tried in file order and at most ONE fires per cell per tick — put specific rules (acid+stone) before generic tag rules (acid+tag:dissolvable). Three shapes: pair {self,neighbor,...}, decay {self,decay:true,becomes}, emit {self,emit,dir}. neighbor accepts a material id, tag:xxx, or any (optionally filtered by neighborClass). dir: any|up|down|side. Products: selfBecomes/neighborBecomes/becomes; 'air' deletes. "drying": true marks a rule as the world's abstraction of matter soaking into the ground or drying in the open (blood -> air), not chemistry: the world runs it as authored, the alchemy bench never fires it on matter inside a vessel. CPU-only (MaterialDef::ruleFx drying), it touches no GPU data and cannot move the world hash. Every other rule that turns its self into air still runs on the bench in an OPEN vessel (smoke fades, a vapour disperses); in a STOPPERED vessel no decay to air fires except a fast transient (spark, glare: at least a tenth of the chance scale a tick).

reactions.note: -------- fire: short-lived rising flame; doused by water --------

-------- RAIN (weather::SimRainWord, TickParams.weatherRain) --------
Every burning material carries a "rain" douse beside its extinguisher douse: it fires only on a rain-exposed cell (it sees the sky, or a side face opens onto a cell that does) while it rains, at chance x (rain/255)^2 -- so a drizzle barely touches a fire and a storm puts it out. The product is the extinguisher's product. The other half is "rainDamped" on every COMBUSTION ignition (tag:hot rules on fuel; not water boiling, ice melting or flesh searing): on an exposed cell its chance is cut by max(rain, ground wetness) x weather.rainIgniteDamp, so rain slows a fire's spread at once and wet ground stays slow to catch for about weather.drySeconds after. Bodies and limbs count as exposed (sim/reactcpu.h).
-------- smoke & steam: fade; steam condenses into rain --------

-------- combustion: each flammable defines its burn character --------
THE IGNITION CHANCE IS HOW FAST FIRE SPREADS THROUGH THE FUEL; the decay rules further down are how long a lit voxel takes to be consumed. They are separate levers and this note exists because they are easy to confuse. Wood/bark were slowed 1.5x here (18 -> 12, birch 22 -> 15, staff 16 -> 11) so a fire creeps up a trunk instead of running it; the ember decays below are UNCHANGED, so a lit log still burns out on the same schedule it always did.

-------- neighborChance: the FLOATING flame is a weak igniter --------
Every ignition rule below is `neighbor: tag:hot`, and `fire` -- the gas that rises off every burning voxel and drifts through the air, the thing that reads on screen as embers floating up from a blaze -- carries that tag alongside the stationary heat sources (ember, lava, a burning leaf, burning cloth and flesh). So a single drifting flame that brushed a tree, a robe or a grass slope lit it at the same rate as a bed of coals pressed against it, and a campfire's plume set light to everything downwind of it.

`"neighborChance": { "fire": 0.0625 }` on a rule says: this rule's chance, but a SIXTEENTH of it when the hot neighbour is fire. It shipped at an eighth; the owner halved it again on 2026-09-03 ('the fire voxels, the ones that move through the air, have 50% even less chance to catch things') in the same change that let a burning limb heat the limb next to it (Mob::BuildCrossLimbHeat) -- the drifting flame was the only path between a torso and the legs, and now that it is not, it can be as weak as it reads. THE ONE THING THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN is the skin sear (`skin + tag:hot -> flesh_cooked`, no neighborChance), so a body in a fire column still cooks at the same rate; what got rarer is a passing flame lighting the robe. The loader (src/sim/materials.cpp ExpandNeighborChance) compiles it away into two rules the kernels already understand -- the base rule re-pointed at a synthetic tag (hot minus fire) and an exact-neighbour fire rule at the scaled chance -- so nothing on the GPU or in the body evaluator learned a new field, and a new hot material is covered without remembering a second tag. ONLY IGNITION carries it: a rule whose product is a burning material. The steam / melt / mite rules on tag:hot are untouched (a flame over water still steams it), the skin SEAR is untouched (a lick of flame still cooks the surface; flammability is the minCount-3 decay, which counts hot faces and has no per-material weight), and it never touches how long anything burns. The stationary sources keep the authored rate, so a burning log still lights the log beside it exactly as before -- what changed is that the flames rising OFF it are no longer the thing that spreads the fire. THE COST, measured and accepted by the owner: the flame a burning voxel emits DOWNWARD is fire too, and it was fire's only path across an air gap, so the fire-down gate's arm B (a slab of leaves lighting the slab one cell of air below it) fell from saturating to ~9% -- a canopy with air between its layers now burns its top and leaves the layers below a gap alone. fire-down is carried as known-failing in tests/baseline.json for that reason; the fix, if one is ever wanted, is a downward product that does not float, not a bigger fire multiplier.

foliage is CONSUMED and leaves no ash: a burning canopy should vanish in flame, not decay into thousands of ash voxels raining through the crown. Chances are high because leaves are thin fuel; the burn is bounded by the canopy itself (leaf_burning leaves nothing that grows). ALL FOLIAGE CHANCES WERE CUT 3x on owner report that a crown went up too readily (leaves 225->75->25, needles 380->127, autumn 400->133): a tree should catch and take a while about it rather than flashing over the instant an ember touches it. THEN, on 2026-09-08, THE SPREAD BETWEEN THE THREE FUELS WAS DELETED: the owner's report was that only autumn leaves burned like leaves and the other two families barely caught at all, so green leaves went 25 -> 133 and needles 127 -> 133 and every tree-leaf family now catches at autumn's rate. The old ratio was authored as a read -- dry needle and dead leaf catching several times faster than green foliage, a pine forest frightening and an oak wood merely flammable -- and green leaves at a fifth of autumn's chance turned out to be the wrong end of it to have tuned: 25 per-mille per hot face is a crown that smoulders at the ignition point instead of one that burns. If the families are ever to differ again, do it by moving needles and autumn UP from 133, not by moving green leaves back down. These are how fast a crown CATCHES; how far the fire then travels is leaf_burning's decay total below, which is the better lever and did not move.

WHAT DID CHANGE IS THE PRODUCT. These rules used to read `selfBecomes: fire`, and that is why a lit tree cooked the top of the crown and left the bottom-most layer of leaves alone. `fire` is a GAS that rises with probability 1 in calm air, so a burnt leaf turned itself into the one thing that immediately leaves the neighbourhood: the leaf directly below got exactly one 2.5% roll before its only heat source floated away, and nothing would ever bring heat back down to it. Wood never had this problem because it ignites to `ember`, a stationary tag:hot solid. Foliage now does the same through `leaf_burning`, which is ember-for-leaves: it stands still, cooks all six of its faces for the length of its burn, and decays to air rather than ash. Spread is now a front with a direction-free shape instead of a rising plume.

THE SHADE RAMPS BURN LIKE WHAT THEY ARE. assets/editor/treegen.js bakes each foliage and bark family as a three-material ramp (dark / plain / lit) so a crown has form; combustion in this file is authored BY NAME, not by tag, so a ramp member with no rule of its own is a leaf that will not catch. Same chance as its plain sibling in every case -- these are lighting tiers, not different fuels, and a canopy that burned in stripes would be worse than one that did not burn at all.

-------- leaf_burning: ember for leaves. Stands still, cooks its neighbours in every direction, leaves nothing --------
THE DECAY TOTAL IS THE WHOLE TUNING SURFACE HERE. 80 per-mille is ~12.5 ticks (0.4 s) per leaf voxel, against `fire`'s ~6, and that number is chosen for reach rather than for looks: every leaf now catches at 133 per-mille per hot face (2026-09-08; it was 25 for the green family when this paragraph was first written, and the arithmetic below is the reason that number was a problem), so a neighbour exposed for 12.5 ticks catches with probability 1 - 0.867^12.5 = 83%, and a leaf with four foliage neighbours passes the fire on ~3.3 times before it is spent. Comfortably above unity: a crown that catches anywhere burns through everywhere, which is the read the owner asked for. At the old 25 it was ~1.1 -- barely propagating, and a front that marginal dies out against any gap in the canopy, which is exactly what a green tree that would not burn looked like. It is bounded the way this file has always bounded foliage, by the fuel being CONSUMED into something that authors no rules, not by the growth factor. Per TICK the growth is 4 x 0.133 = 0.53, still inside rule 2's subcritical ceiling.

Cut this total and the front stalls out in the interior of a canopy; raise it and a single spark takes the whole forest. It is the one number to reach for if a burning tree feels wrong, and it is a much better lever than the ignition chances above, which the owner has already tuned twice and which control how readily a crown catches at all rather than how far the fire then travels.

No ash branch AT ALL, deliberately, where cloth and flesh both keep a rare one: a crown is tens of thousands of voxels and even a 0.33 per-mille ash branch would rain a floor of it under every burnt tree. Smoke is the visible residue instead.

Douse first, then emit, then the decays -- the ember ordering, for the ember reason: water must beat the burn to the tick.

THE THREE EMIT RULES ARE ONE RULE WITH A PREFERENCE, and the shape is load-bearing. An emit rule only fires into an AIR neighbour: sim_step.wgsl's RK_EMIT arm scans the allowed directions and falls through to the next rule when none of them is air. So `up` is tried first and gets the whole chance whenever the flame has somewhere to go, which keeps a burning crown looking like a burning crown; and when the cell above is more canopy -- i.e. exactly in the interior, where the old model delivered no heat downward at all -- the up rule is skipped entirely and the down and side rules get their full roll. The flame licks down only where it cannot go up, which is both the right picture and the cheap one.

Down at half of up rather than at parity because this is still fire: the asymmetry is real physics, it just should not have been TOTAL. The old model was 90:0.

-------- pine_burning / autumn_burning: leaf_burning, once per foliage family --------
Three burning-leaf materials rather than one, and the reason is the RENDERER, not the sim: a burning leaf keeps the palette of the leaf it was and pulses toward the flame colour (materials.json "burnTint", common.wgsl burnTint), and the voxel word has no bits left to remember which leaf a burning one used to be, so the material id is the memory. The three families' dark / plain / lit shade tiers collapse onto the plain tier's burning material -- a lighting tier is not worth a material. EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS leaf_burning's, deliberately: these are the same fuel, and the fire-down gate's argument about reach (12.5 ticks of exposure per leaf, ~1.1 hand-offs per leaf) is made once, above, for all three. Change one, change all three.

OIL IS HOW EASILY AN OILED THING CATCHES (2026-09-24). This one rule runs for a pool of oil AND, through the coat rule (DESIGN.md §6), for every oiled voxel, ground or body: each firing spends one level of the coat, throws a flame into an open face, and (clause 2c) makes the flame ON the voxel, which catches as its own catch form -- oiled grass to fire, an oiled plank to ember, oiled skin to flesh_burning. So this chance is the owner's "oil should catch fire easily in all scenarios", one number for all of them. 350 -> 700 on that ask: at 350 an oiled forearm under lava burnt 14,246 voxel-ticks against the pre-W2-J2 22,920; at 700 21,728; at 1000 21,181 (saturated: past ~700 the limit is heat reaching the oiled skin, not the oil catching). Compiled through combustion.spreadPct like every ignition, and a drifting flame lights oil at neighborChance x combustion.flamePct of it.

A POOL OF OIL CATCHES AS oil_burning, not as a flash of fire (owner, 2026-09-30: burn 'like ether gas ... for a good 10ish seconds'). A DECAY gated on a hot face (scaleByNeighbors tag:hot, scaleMax 1: gated, not scaled) and FIRST in oil's bucket, for one reason: a coat runs only its material's PAIR rules and needs their product to be a flame (sim_step.wgsl coatReact, rules 2-3) -- a liquid product would COVER the cell under an oil coat instead of setting it alight. So the coat keeps the pair rule below, untouched, and the pool rolls this one first. Authored 1000, compiled x combustion.spreadPct (~290 per-mille a tick beside anything hot): extremely flammable, and the burning oil is itself hot, so a front runs through a spill a cell or so a tick. A floating flame gets no discount here (a count ramp has no per-material weight). The pair rule still fires when this roll fails -- about a third of a pool flashes straight to fire, which reads as the flare at the edge of an oil fire.
-------- ember: smolders, licks flame upward, dies to ash; doused back to charwood --------

EVERY EMIT RULE IN THIS FILE USED TO BE dir:up, AND THAT WAS THE BUG. Combined with `fire` being a gas that rises with probability 1 in calm air (gasIntent, sim_step.wgsl), it meant the world had no downward heat path of any kind: the only thing that ever warmed a voxel from above was a stationary tag:hot SOLID touching it directly. Owner report, two symptoms, one cause -- a lit tree cooks the top of its crown and ignores the bottom layer of leaves, and a character whose torso burns through never lights his own legs.

So every up-emit below now has a down sibling at half its chance. The half is not timidity, it is the physics being restored to an asymmetry instead of an absolute: fire really does prefer to go up, it just does not refuse to go down.

WHY THE ORDER IS SAFE. RK_EMIT only fires into an AIR neighbour and falls through to the next rule when no allowed direction is air, so `up` first costs the down rule nothing in the case that matters -- a flame with fuel or ground above it skips the up rule entirely and the down rule rolls at full chance. In the open the up rule wins most ticks and the flame still reads as rising. One caveat worth recording because the two evaluators differ here: MobSystem::BurnOneLimb's emit arm does NOT test the target for air before consuming the rule (it relies on kCellOpIfAir downstream), so on a BODY the down rule gets the residual ~93% of its chance rather than the full amount. That is still hundreds of fire voxels a tick under a burning torso, which is what reaches the legs -- the limb lattices cannot see each other at all, so the world grid is the only channel between them.

The ember stage IS the burn: wood ignites to ember on contact with tag:hot, then smolders here until one of these decay rules retires it. Their SUM is the death rate, so scaling all three together sets burn DURATION without touching how fire spreads (that is the wood+tag:hot ignition rule above, deliberately left fast). Total 7 per-mille vs the old 27 = wood takes ~4x longer to be consumed, ~140 ticks mean. Within that budget ash is ~1/4 of decays and smoke is doubled relative to the old 20:7 ash:smoke split, so a burnt-out fire leaves a scatter of ash rather than a floor of it. Embers also live 4x longer, so each one emits its upward fire ~4x more over its life: fire persists longer without spreading faster.

"burnDuration": true MARKS A RULE AS PART OF THE COMBUSTION CLOCK. Every marked chance is divided by combustion.burnDurationPct at load (src/sim/materials.cpp), so the Combustion tab is one slider over how long anything in the world stays alight, authored once here rather than by hand-editing eighteen chances that have to keep their ratios.

Two kinds of rule carry it, and the second is not obvious. The first is every rule that RETIRES a burning voxel -- ember to ash, smoke or air; burning cloth, linen, hair and flesh to their spent forms. Halving those is the feature.

The second is every RELIGHT rule (charred back to burning). Those are the only rules in the file that put matter BACK into a burning state, so they are the only closed loop in the fire economy, and its gain is (relight chance per tick) x (how long a neighbour stays lit). Scaling the burn duration without scaling these multiplies that gain by the same factor, which is fine at 200% -- measured, the difference at the `mob-burn` corpse was 13 voxels still alight versus 15, i.e. nothing -- and is not fine at the top of the slider, where an unscaled gain would cross 1.0 and the fire would never go out (CLAUDE.md rule 2). This is a CEILING argument, not a fix for anything observed at the default: dividing the relight rules too holds the gain exactly where the author put it at every setting, so the slider changes the CLOCK of the fire and never its shape. A corpse in lava re-flares half as often and stays lit twice as long, which is the same corpse running at half speed.

It is NOT on the ignition rules, the emit rules or the extinguisher rules, and each exclusion is a decision: ignition is how fast fire SPREADS (a separate lever -- see the combustion note at the top of this file -- and leaving it alone is what makes a longer burn also spread further, since a voxel that stays lit twice as long emits its upward flame twice as many times), emit is how much flame a lit voxel SHOWS, and dousing must beat the burn to the tick at any setting.
-------- water vs heat --------

reactions.//neighborChance: A burning oil slick FLOATS on water and burns ~10 s: at the full 180 it would boil a hole in the lake under itself. x0.03 (~5 per-mille) lets the surface simmer.

reactions.note: -------- lava: crusts against water, melts sand. Deliberately NOT tag:meltable: glass must be stable next to lava or the pool rim remelts its own crust forever and never sleeps --------

Lava BURNS AWAY organic matter it touches (2026-09-23): flesh, cloth, leaves, grass go up as flame outright rather than only being ignited through their own tag:hot rules. This is what makes a lava coat on a body DISINTEGRATE it (mob.cpp BurnOneLimb section 3 runs the coat's own rules against the voxel under it) and what makes wading in a pool eat the feet (section 2). Bounded like every contact rule: it consumes what it touches and grows nothing.
-------- molten glass: cools to glass, quenched instantly by water --------
-------- acid erosion chain (stone->gravel->sand->gone); glass is immune --------

ACID EATS MEAT FAR FASTER THAN IT EATS ROCK, and this is the rule that says so. Ordered BEFORE the generic tag:dissolvable rule below, per the file's specific-before-generic convention, so mineral erosion keeps its old slow chain and only organics get the fast one.

WHY IT MATTERS OUT OF PROPORTION TO ITS SIZE: this rule reaches a BODY. mob.cpp's inbound pass evaluates acid's own rules FROM the grid cell ONTO each body voxel it touches (the same direction the GPU evaluates them), so skin, flesh, bone, cloth and leather -- all tag:organic -- are eaten by this line and by nothing that had to be written for them. At the old shared 45 per-mille a limb at skinScale 8 lost about 4.5% of ONE sub-voxel layer per tick, roughly two seconds per layer and the better part of a minute for an arm, which is what 'acid does not do nearly enough damage' actually was. At 250 a layer went in about ten ticks; halved to 125 (owner, 2026-09-23: disintegrates flesh twice too fast), about twenty -- still five times rock's 25.

Steel is unaffected because `steel` carries no tag:organic and no tag:dissolvable -- armour still protects, and still for the reason equipment.h states: not a resist number, an absence of the tag.

PACKAGE E (2026-09-27) CUT THIS 125 -> 85, AND THE TOTAL DID NOT MOVE: the 40 went to an appended `acid + tag:organic -> noxious_gas` (the end of the file), so an organic voxel is still eaten at about the same per-tick rate (~16%) but about a THIRD of what acid eats now comes off as green fume instead of vanishing. Package C measured the old share at about one in ten, which read as a pool that barely smoked.

ACID PITS IRON, SLOWLY. The plate set (assets/items/iron_*.json) is `iron`, a material that carries no dissolvable tag on purpose: the two tag rules above would otherwise apply as well, and a rule that fails its roll does not stop the next one from being tried. So iron's whole acid behaviour is this one line -- 10 per-mille a tick, against 250 for the organics a body is made of, which is what makes a suit of it a real answer to a pool of acid rather than a slower way to die in one. Steel stays IMMUNE (no rule, no tag); that is what a sword is made of and what armor-react measures.

APPENDED after acid's other rules rather than placed specific-before-generic, and deliberately: the convention exists so a specific rule wins over a tag rule that would ALSO match, and nothing else matches iron. Placing it earlier would renumber every acid rule after it, and rule index is part of the reaction RNG stream (mob.cpp's inbound pass, sim_step's bucket loop) -- a re-roll of every acid reaction in the world for a rule that fires only against a material worldgen never places. This way the determinism hash does not move.
-------- cold: creeping freeze, melting, snow compaction --------
-------- plants: the sandspiel signature. plant grows into water; seeds sprout stalks that race hardening vs growth; stems rarely branch; tips bloom --------
germination is daylight-only (day/night cycle). The chance is unchanged, so a seed sown in the morning behaves exactly as before; one sown at night simply waits for dawn.

stem growth must stay decisively subcritical: mean stalk = up/(up-decays) cells, branches-per-stalk = stalk * side/(side+decays). At 380/4/78 that is ~6-cell stalks with R~0.3 branches — the epidemic dies out and chunks sleep. Raising side or up can make growth self-sustaining forever (measured: 400/6/52 never settles).

BOUNDED BY DAYLIGHT (2026-09-23). Ungated, this rule held its chunk awake whenever any side of any vine was air (an EMIT that finds its cell sets keepAwake), i.e. forever for a hanging vine, and made flowers from nothing at 2 per mille per vine the whole time. `when: day` makes it light-gated, and a light-gated rule never sets keepAwake (sim_step doReactions), so a vine no longer holds a chunk awake by itself; it flowers only on daylight ticks its chunk is awake for another reason. Total output stays bounded at one flower per open side (4 per vine voxel) because a flower fills the cell it is emitted into. `vine emit vine down` is unchanged: its keep-awake ends when the tip reaches something.
-------- fungus: creeps over everything organic --------
-------- mites: wandering critters — eat the garden, breed on plants, drown, expire --------
-------- cloner-style sources and the void drain --------
blood dries away so pools go back to sleep (PLAN #B5, rule 2). DRYING: it soaks into the ground / dries in the open, which a flask has neither of -- the alchemy bench never fires it inside a vessel.

======== DAY/NIGHT INTERACTIONS ========================================
These carry the light conditions added with the day/night cycle:
  "needsSky": true   the cell must have open sky above it (bounded probe up)
  "when": "day"      only while the sun is up  |  "night" only while it is down
  "minLight": 0-255  a floor on daylight strength (255 = only at high noon)

All three are integer and derived from the tick-based day phase, so they are
as deterministic as every other rule (CLAUDE.md rule 1).

SLEEP DISCIPLINE (rule 2): a rule whose light condition is UNMET does not hold
its chunk awake, so a pond sleeps all night instead of spinning. The engine
wakes every chunk on the tick daylight switches on or off (Simulation::
EncodeWakeAll), which is a few ticks per in-game day. Chances are kept low so
these are a slow background weathering, not a strobe.

-------- sun + water: evaporation --------
SPREAD WATER burns off in the sun; BODIES of water do not. This is the mirror
image of the freezing rule below, and it is the whole reason evaporation is
interesting rather than just a slow leak on every pond.

The chance is scaled by how many of the six face neighbours are NOT water
("neighbor": "water" + "invert": true), with a minCount of 4 — so a cell needs
to be mostly OUT of the water before the sun can take it:

  - 0 non-water (deep water)               never. Fully enclosed.
  - 1 non-water (flat pond surface, air     never. This is the case that
    above and water on all five other       matters: a pond's surface is NOT
    sides)                                  consumed, so ponds are stable.
  - 2-3 non-water (surface near a bank)    never. Still reads as "pond".
  - 4 non-water (a rim cell, a thin sheet) base rate, ~1 real minute.
  - 5 non-water (nearly isolated)          1.3x
  - 6 non-water (a lone droplet on stone)  3x, ~40 real seconds.

So rain puddles and splash thrown onto hot rock steam away while the lake they
came from sits there. Because a pond can only ever lose cells from its rim,
and losing a rim cell exposes the next one, a SHALLOW puddle still dries up
from its edges inward — it just takes minutes, not seconds.

minLight 120 confines it to the middle of the day (the rule is live for about
a quarter of the cycle), and needsSky keeps water in caves and under canopy
intact. Strictly consumptive (water -> steam -> mostly air), so it is
subcritical by construction: it can only ever remove water.

-------- steam condenses into rain --------
Steam already decays to water at 3 per mille everywhere. This adds a NIGHT
bias: cold night air condenses it faster, so morning fog burns off and evening
air turns to dew. Still net-consumptive of steam.

-------- growth follows the light --------
Plants only put on growth in daylight. The existing stem/sprout rules are left
alone (their subcritical budget is carefully tuned — see the stem note above);
these are the ADDITIONAL daylight-only behaviours.

Grass creeping onto lit soil is the one rule here that creates new matter, so
it is the one to watch: it is capped by needsSky (only the exposed top surface
of the ground qualifies) and by requiring a soil neighbour, so the frontier is
a 2D surface, not a volume, and it terminates when the surface is covered. At
3 per mille it spreads about a cell per 10 in-game seconds of daylight.

flowers close at night and reopen by day (petal <-> flower is a pure
palette swap between two inert solids, so it cannot cascade)

-------- fungus prefers the dark --------
The existing fungus rule spreads over organics at 7 per mille regardless of
light. This adds a faster NIGHT spread, so a cellar or a moonlit forest floor
creeps visibly while a sunlit meadow barely does. Same bounded frontier as the
existing rule (it converts organics, and organics do not regrow).

FUNGUS ROTS AWAY (2026-09-23, CLAUDE.md rule 2: bound every emergent process). Without this a fungus voxel was permanent and converted every organic neighbour, grass included, so a patch crept over a whole meadow or forest. The bound is a decay to dirt, tried AFTER both spread rules so it only rolls on ticks the cell did not spread. Expected neighbours converted over one fungus voxel's life = p / ((1 - p) q) with q = 0.020: at night p = 1 - (1 - 0.007)(1 - 0.009) = 0.0159, giving 0.81; by day p = 0.007, giving 0.35. Both < 1, so a fungus front is subcritical and dies out, leaving dirt (soil, which grass can re-cover by day). Mean life 1/q = 50 ticks, during which the unconditional decay keeps the chunk awake; that ends when the cell rots.

-------- sunlight through glass ignites tinder --------
The magnifying-glass trick. Requires the dry foliage to be under open sky AND
touching glass AND near peak sun, so it is rare enough to be a discovery
rather than a hazard that burns the world down every noon. Fire is already
bounded (it decays in ~6 ticks and leaves nothing that regrows).

-------- NOT IMPLEMENTED: overnight dew on foliage --------
A night-time "leaves emit steam upward" rule was tried twice and REMOVED both
times. Recording it here so it is not re-attempted a third time.

Attempt 1 — plain emit. doReactions() set keepAwake as soon as an emit rule
found an adjacent air cell, before rolling its chance, so every leaf with air
above it pinned its chunk awake all night: 292/32768 chunks active after 2900
settle ticks, against a budget of 32 (CLAUDE.md rule 2).

Attempt 2 — after making light-gated rules skip keepAwake (that change was
kept; it is correct and the other gated rules need it). Still 250 chunks
awake, now as a permanent steam plume: every canopy leaf is a SOURCE, the
steam it emits is a gas that moves every tick and re-dirties its chunk, and
emission outpaces steam's decay. Awake chunks were a vertical column at fixed
x,z — a plume, not a settling neighbourhood.

The lesson is rule 2's: a permanent emitter has no terminus, so no chance
value makes it settle. Dew needs a FINITE source — e.g. a dew material that
leaves deposit once and consume, or a decay on something that runs out.
Left out rather than shipped breaking the sleep guarantee.
-------- BODIES: per-voxel burning (docs/PLAN_body_reactivity.md) --------

These materials only ever exist as MOB and ITEM geometry, so until now they were tagged flammable and had no rules at all: a creature could stand in a bonfire forever. Nothing below is mob-specific. MobSystem::BurnLimbs and DebrisSystem::BurnBodies run this same authored table over body voxels through the CPU mirror in sim/reactcpu.h, so a burning limb, a severed burning arm, a dropped burning staff and a cloth voxel that settled into the grid all behave identically.

THE SHAPE OF THE MECHANIC. Cloth catches from ONE hot neighbour at about 8x flesh's rate; flesh does not catch at all until THREE of its six faces are hot. That is authored as a decay rule with scaleByNeighbors, because a pair rule's neighbour fields are already spoken for by its partner. The minCount is the load-bearing number: it is what makes a lone ember on a shoulder gutter out while a wide burning front races, i.e. the difference between 'the mob is on fire' as a boolean and fire as a front with a width.

CLOTH: catches from a single hot face and is CONSUMED, leaving holes and scorched rag. All three robe materials share one burning state so the burn character is authored once and a new fabric inherits it by naming cloth_burning as its product.
Leather is fabric that resists: the same burning state at one eighth the catch rate. The whole 'a leather jerkin buys you seconds a robe does not' mechanic is this one number.

Douse FIRST, then emit, then the decays -- the ember ordering, for the ember reason: water must beat the burn to the tick, and a voxel that spent its tick licking flame upward should not also consume itself. Total decay 39 per-mille is about 26 ticks (0.9 s) per cloth voxel, so a robe burns away over seconds instead of vanishing in one frame.

The ash branch is deliberately 15x rarer than it first shipped (5 -> 0.33 per-mille): a burning robe is a lot of voxels and at 5 per-mille it buried the wearer's feet in ash. Its old share went to the 'becomes air' branch so the 39 per-mille total -- and therefore the burn DURATION -- is unchanged; only the fraction of cloth that survives as matter moved. Ash from a garment is now a scatter, not a pile.

BURNT FIRST, THEN NOTHING (owner, 2026-09-25: 'when you set someone on fire the clothes just become burnt; it should turn to burnt -> nothing if the burnt clothes are still on fire, which should destroy clothing and further light skin on fire'). Burning cloth no longer vanishes straight to air: all of its 39 per-mille (less the ash sliver) now lands on cloth_charred, so the garment visibly BLACKENS as the front passes, and the char is what goes to nothing -- while it is still in the fire -- in the rule below. The total is unchanged, so a voxel stays alight exactly as long as before and the combustion slider reads the same.

CHARRED RAG STILL IN THE FIRE BURNS TO NOTHING. One hot face is enough -- the burning cloth beside it, the flame it licks up, the wearer's own burning flesh under it (the shell reads a burning limb as heat across the joint) -- and more faces burn it faster, up to four. With nothing hot left around it the char is inert, so a garment that was put out, or that the fire has moved on from, hangs as scorched rag instead of evaporating. It REPLACES the old three-face relight (charred -> burning): that was the only closed loop in the cloth chain and it mostly left a burnt garment in place; this ends the chain in air and grows nothing, so it is subcritical by construction (CLAUDE.md rule 2). burnDuration, because it retires fuel. The HOLE it leaves is the point for the wearer: a char voxel over the skin reads as cold cloth to the worn-occlusion probe forever, and air lets the fire through.
HAIR: catches almost on contact and is gone in about 4 ticks. One material and three rules, and it is the clearest single read that a character is on fire.

-------- LINEN: the peasant wardrobe's cloth, which now BURNS AWAY like every garment (2026-09-25) --------
Everything linen_burning makes is cloth_charred, so a smock blackens and then burns to nothing while it is still in the fire, exactly as a robe does (see the cloth chain above). The paragraph below is the history of why this chain once ended in the inert linen_charred instead: the base human's UNDERWEAR was linen then, and burning it away undressed the character. The shorts have been their own material since 2026-09-23 (`undercloth`, which chars to linen_charred and stays -- see its block below), so the reason no longer applies to linen and the owner asked for burnt clothes to go. linen_charred remains, as the undercloth's terminus only.

HISTORY: A near-copy of the cloth chain above with one branch deleted, and the deletion is the mechanic. cloth_burning is CONSUMED (26.67 of its 39 per-mille go to air), which is right for a robe -- a burnt robe should hang in rags. It is wrong for the one garment the character is wearing UNDER everything: burning it away undresses them, and 'the player caught fire and is now naked' is a worse read than any amount of scorching.

So linen_burning has exactly one decay branch and it lands on linen_charred, which authors no rules at all. Same 39 per-mille total, so it burns for the same LENGTH of time as a robe and responds to the burn-duration slider identically; only the destination moved. It still catches at cloth's rate, still emits fire upward while alight, so it still spreads a fire and still cooks the flesh underneath through the ordinary table -- what it cannot do is disappear.

FLESH: sears on contact, ignites only under a WIDE front. skin -> flesh_cooked is a plain pair rule, so a single lick of flame cooks the surface and a creature can be seared without being destroyed. Ignition is the scaled decay below.

IGNITION WAS RAISED 9.75x IN TWO PASSES (40 -> 130 -> 390) on owner report that a body was not flammable enough. THE SEAR WAS NOT, and the attempt to raise it is worth recording because it was wrong for a reason that is easy to repeat: skin -> flesh_cooked is a COLOUR CHANGE, not combustion, so raising it makes a body look cooked faster without making it any more likely to catch. It also broke the one comparison this whole section is built on -- at sear 220 vs cloth's 200 the flesh reacted to a single hot face MORE eagerly than the cloth over it, which inverts 'cloth catches at about 8x flesh's rate' -- and the mob-burn gate caught it as cloth and skin halving on the same tick. Flammability is the decay below; the sear stays at 90. THE MINCOUNT DID NOT MOVE and must not: 3 is the reason a lone ember on a shoulder gutters out, and it is provable rather than tuned (see the next note). At 390 with scaleMax 4 the scaled chance is 858 per-mille at the minCount-3 threshold and saturates at 1000 under a full six-face front, i.e. cooked flesh under a real fire ignites within a tick or two -- the SEAR (90) is now what paces a body catching alight, not the ignition. Raising the chance makes a real fire take hold quickly; lowering the count would make ANY spark take hold, which is a different and much worse game.

minCount 3 is deliberate and provable: a lone burning voxel plus the single fire cell it emits reach 2, so one ignited voxel cannot restart itself no matter how the dice fall. Three simultaneously hot faces means a real fire -- or burning cloth lying against the skin, which is exactly how a clothing layer is supposed to kill you.

ON A BODY THE COUNT IS TAKEN AT WORLD PITCH, and without that this minCount means something entirely different from what the paragraph above says.

In the grid, fire and flesh are cells of the same size, so "three of my six faces are hot" really is "I am half-surrounded by fire". A mob or the player is a lattice EIGHT TIMES FINER (skinScale 8), and five of a skin sub-voxel's six faces are its own flesh however large the fire outside is -- so the count is 1 on a flat surface, 2 on a convex edge, and reaches 3 only on a convex CORNER. Measured over a 90-tick immersion of the bare `human` rig: world-facing faces 0:711k 1:465k 2:190k 3:26k, 92% of every ignition roll refused, 11 of 22,775 flesh voxels lost. On screen that is a character who sears brown all over and turns black ONLY along the outlines of its limbs.

So MobSystem::BurnOneLimb reads the four world cells TANGENTIAL to each exposed face and lets that face count for as much as the fire against it is WIDE (1..5), taken as a max against the ordinary lattice count. One cell of flame is still 1 and still gutters out -- the claim the paragraph above makes is intact, and is now true of bodies as well as of the grid -- while a wall of flame is 5 and takes hold. That is a change to WHERE THE SIX NEIGHBOURS COME FROM, which sim/reactcpu.h names as the one part of the two evaluators that legitimately differs; every authored number here, including this minCount, is untouched and shared. 9.8% -> 23.7% of flesh past the sear at 90 ticks, 45% cinder at 400. Guarded by mobBurnFleshCharPctMin in tests/baseline.json, which exists because the gate counted flesh_cooked -- a SEAR at one hot face, not combustion -- as "charred", so a body that only seared scored the same as one that burned.

FLESH 30% LESS FLAMMABLE (owner, 2026-09-23): BOTH doors into the chain take the same 0.7 -- the sear 90 -> 63 on skin, flesh and muscle, and this ignition 390 -> 273 -- because either one alone moves only half of 'how fast a body catches'. The sear paces a body under a real fire (the ignition saturates at a full front either way), the ignition is what a partial front (3..4 hot faces) rolls against. Cloth still catches at ~3x flesh's sear. The 90 / 390 figures in the two notes above are the history; these are the numbers.

Burning flesh almost always CHARS IN PLACE rather than disappearing: charred is a solid, so the limb keeps its shape and reads as burnt instead of eaten away. That is what leaves a recognisable blackened corpse -- and, where a limb burned through, bone, which has no fire rules at all and therefore survives by construction.

The ash branch takes the same 15x cut as cloth's above (8 -> 0.53 per-mille) and for the same reason, with its old share folded into the char branch so the 50 per-mille total and the burn duration are unchanged. Burning bodies still shed ash, just rarely enough that it reads as soot rather than as the body dissolving into a heap.

DEEP CHAR. flesh_charred is what one pass of flame leaves: dark, but still brown and still meat. Fire that KEEPS coming takes it one stage further to flesh_cinder -- near-black, crisp, and inert. That is the difference between 'this body was in a fire' and 'this body was torched', and it is a stage rather than a palette jitter because it has different RULES: cinder authors none at all, so it can neither re-ignite nor be driven further, and a corpse burned this far is permanently black and permanently settled.

It sits ABOVE the relight rule on purpose. Both roll every tick on the same voxel and the first to fire wins, so at 20 vs 8 a body under a sustained blaze cinders about two and a half times more often than it flares back up. That makes the char chain CONVERGE under fire instead of cycling charred -> burning -> charred, which is strictly better for rule 2 than the relight rule alone: the terminus is an inert material rather than a coin flip that never ends.

minCount 3 rather than the relight rule's 4 because this is a much smaller claim -- 'the fire is still on me', not 'the fire is hot enough to restart spent fuel' -- and because a lone ember still cannot reach 3 (see the minCount note above). Not marked burnDuration: nothing here is alight, so the burn-duration slider has no business in it.

Charred flesh relights only under a full four-face front, which in practice means lava or a sustained blaze. Without that floor a burnt corpse is a permanent low-grade emitter and its chunk never sleeps (CLAUDE.md rule 2).

-------- UNDERCLOTH: the base human's shorts, which BURN AS FLESH and still read as shorts --------
The human's underwear used to be `linen`, which is also the peasant wardrobe's cloth, so it caught at cloth's rate (200 vs skin's sear) and burned as a garment. Owner, 2026-09-23: it should be flesh in every respect but its look. So it is its own chain that copies flesh's NUMBERS rule for rule -- sear 63, ignition 273 at minCount 3 / scaleMax 4, 500 douse, 70/35 emit, 50 per-mille burn to char, 20 cinder, 8 relight at minCount 4 -- through stages that keep linen's colours, so a torched character still shows scorched shorts rather than reading naked at the first sear (the reason linen got its own id in the first place). Two deliberate differences, both visual: the 0.53 per-mille ash branch is folded into the char branch (a garment that falls away as ash is the naked read again), and the cinder terminus is linen_charred (no rules, so it is exactly as inert as flesh_cinder).

The .vox still paints the shorts as `linen` -- a new id is past the 127-entry palette ceiling -- and the human sidecar's `anatomy.garmentsBecome` rewrites them to `undercloth` at load (MobSystem, after anatomy::Resolve). Keep these numbers in step with the flesh chain above: they are a copy, not a reference.
A dropped wooden staff is a debris body with a micro brick and BurnBodies runs this table over it, so 'fire lights the item you dropped' costs exactly this one rule.

-------- BUILDING MATERIALS (PLAN_world_editor P2) --------
One ignition rule each, and NOTHING else: the burn itself is the product's. Wood-kind (plank, door_wood, timber) ignite to `ember` exactly as `wood` does, so a burning house smoulders, drops ash and is doused by water on ember's own rules (a doused ember reverts to `wood`, which is what a charred board is). Straw-kind (thatch, straw_bed) ignite to `leaf_burning`, the stationary flame foliage uses, which burns to nothing: a thatched roof fire takes the roof away rather than leaving a straw-coloured ghost of it. Chances sit against wood's 12: boards and a door leaf 12, heavy timber 8 (a 0.2 m beam), thatch 60 and a straw tick 90 (dry straw catches from a spark, still well under green leaves' 133 so a roof takes a moment). Daub, cobble, flagstone and roof_tile have no rule: they do not burn. (A tag rule would be the tidier spelling, but the compiler takes `self` as a material NAME only -- sim/materials.cpp FindMaterial -- and that is C++.)

ANATOMY. `flesh` and `muscle` are the interior layers the human's anatomy recipe bakes under its skin (assets/editor/anatomy.js). They enter the skin's burn chain at the same chance, on the same entry rule, so once fire has charred the skin off a limb the layer it exposes cooks on the same clock rather than sitting there pink and inert. Bone deliberately has NO rule here -- see the note above the flesh_cooked chain.

-------- rot: rotflesh spreads to adjacent living tissue in the world grid --------
The body-side infection (Mob::InfectStep) runs every rotflesh voxel on one per-voxel rule at the rot's `spread` (gore.infectSpreadRate, per voxel per second). These rules are the GRID-SIDE mirror: rotflesh that has settled into the world (a severed limb's remains, a corpse's puddle) infects any flesh, skin or muscle it touches, and `infectSpread: true` makes the loader REPLACE the authored chance with that same number spread over six faces (c = spread * 1000 / 180 per-mille a face a tick, sim/materials.cpp) -- one rate for the rot, body and world. Bone is deliberately immune.

======== ALCHEMY CHEMISTRY, IN THE WORLD (2026-09-27, docs/PLAN_alchemy_chemistry.md package A) ========
Everything below is APPENDED at the end of the file, so each rule lands at the END of its material's bucket: rule index is part of the reaction RNG stream (hash3(rnd, ri, slot)), and appending re-rolls nothing that was already authored -- including the new rules on OLD materials (acid, lye's neutralization) that sit after acid's iron rule.

EFFECTS. A rule may carry "effects": [ {"kind": "explode", "radius": r, "power": p} ]. The rule still writes its products exactly as any rule does; the effect is what ELSE happens. The CA cannot run a blast, so it reports the firing (sim_step.wgsl reactFxNote -> the pageFaults record's per-tick block -> the snapshot ring, fixed latency) and game/session.cpp turns it into a real ExplosionOp through the grenade path: crater, body carve, debris impulse, rig launch, plus a short flash of fire and a puff of smoke laid into the crater the tick after. A body the rule fires ON (mob.cpp's inbound pass: sodium beside a bleeding wound) blasts at the body voxel. BOUNDED: at most 4 reaction blasts a tick, a firing inside a blast already issued this tick is merged into it, and the GPU record keeps 16 candidates a tick chosen order-free -- so a lump of sodium in a lake is a few bangs, not a hundred. radius <= 20 (kMaxExplosionRadius); a grenade is radius 13 power 380 for scale. Kinds the world does not handle (flash, eject, shock, burst -- the alchemy bench's) are ignored here.

IGNITION SCALING, AGAIN. A rule whose selfBecomes is a heat source is an ignition to the loader and is multiplied by combustion.spreadPct (29% as shipped) -- sodium and hydrogen catching fire below are, and their authored chances are written knowing it. Salt MELTING is too (molten_salt is hot), which is why its authored 30 reads as ~9 per-mille.

-------- sodium: explodes in water --------
Real: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2 + heat, violently. So the sodium cell becomes HYDROGEN (which the blast's own fire may then pop -- a second, smaller bang is right) and the water beside it becomes LYE. Weaker blasts in the other wet things. No fire as a direct product on purpose: that would make these ignitions to the loader (x spreadPct); the flame comes from the explosion's aftermath instead. The pile is consumed as it reacts, so a lump in a lake burns out in a few seconds.
Steam only fizzes: a sodium grain in a cloud of steam turns to hydrogen without a bang. Then heat: sodium burns (a real alkali-metal fire).

-------- hydrogen: the lightest gas; pops near a flame or a spark --------
The ignition is authored at 400 and compiled at x spreadPct (~116 per-mille): a hydrogen cloud touching a flame goes off within a few ticks, and each pop is fire that lights the next shell -- a chain the blast cap (4 a tick, merged by radius) and the fuel itself bound. A spark lights it too (tag:electric; not hot, so it is its own rule). Hydrogen and chlorine in daylight make hydrochloric acid with a small bang (the real photochemical H2 + Cl2 reaction). Left alone it simply escapes.

-------- salt melts; molten salt cools; electrolysis --------
Salt melts over heat. molten_salt is itself hot, so without an exception a single hot spot would melt a whole pile through molten salt alone and the pile would then oscillate against its own cooling (rule 2: it would never sleep). The neighborChance exception makes molten salt a very weak melter of salt (2%), fire the usual weak one. Molten salt COOLS back to salt at a rate that rises with how much of its surroundings is NOT hot (an inverted ramp over tag:hot): a pool freezes from its skin inward once the heat is gone, and a vessel on a burner (the alchemy bench's virtual hot neighbour) keeps it molten.

ELECTROLYSIS (the Downs cell, the one real way sodium is made): molten salt touching a spark (tag:electric) splits -- the salt cell becomes sodium, the spark becomes chlorine. Brine electrolysis (chlorine + hydrogen + lye from salt WATER) needs the solute layer's concentration condition and is package B/C's. Salt + water has NO rule here on purpose: salt dissolves into the solute layer once package B lands; until then it sinks like sand.

-------- spark: a discharge that lives a tick or two --------
Decays at 450 per-mille (mean ~2 ticks). Lights what burns beside it WEAKLY -- authored from the spark's side (neighborBecomes fire), so it is not an ignition to the loader's spread knob. Its real job is tag:electric: electrolysis above and hydrogen's pop.

-------- chlorine and noxious gas: toxic --------
Both HURT BODIES through mob.cpp's inbound pass, which runs a world cell's pair rules onto the body voxels it touches (the way acid dissolves a limb): chlorine blisters skin and exposed flesh to flesh_cooked -- a chemical burn, which is a burn stage, so it counts into the burnt fraction that caps a creature's (and the player's) health (DESIGN.md "Blood is health, and burns cap it"). Noxious gas does the same, far more weakly. Neither touches anything a body is not made of.

Chlorine is gas_heavy (materials.h kMatFlagHeavyGas): it SINKS and creeps along the ground, pooling in hollows, instead of rising (sim_step.wgsl stepHeavyGas). It fades slowly (4 per-mille, ~8 s), and bleaches into water very slowly as a weak acid. Noxious gas rises like smoke and fades faster than it (12).

Package D gap-fill (2026-09-27), appended after the decay so no earlier rule's RNG stream moves: the human's shorts are `undercloth`, flesh in everything but look (materials.json), and chlorine passed over them -- they blister to undercloth_seared, flesh_cooked's twin, at chlorine's own rate.
Package D gap-fill (2026-09-27), appended after the decay: noxious gas now reaches everything chlorine does -- bruised skin, muscle bared by a wound, and the undercloth -- at its own weak rate.

-------- acid: dissolves most things, and FUMES --------
Appended after acid's iron rule (rule index is the RNG stream). What acid did not eat before and eats now: crystal (slowly). What it still does not: glass (vials are made of it), steel (armor-react's claim: a sword and plate hold), gold (aqua regia is a later recipe), bone (as authored above), gem_arcane.

EVERY DISSOLUTION FUMES: a share of the voxels acid eats become noxious_gas instead of vanishing -- the dissolvable rule at 5 per-mille against the eating rules' 25-125 is roughly one fuming voxel in ten, which reads as a pool that smokes green while it works rather than as a gas flood. Iron and crystal fume at their own slow rates. On a BODY (the inbound pass and an acid coat) the same rule sends the fume up off the limb.

NEUTRALIZATION: acid meeting lye becomes water (or steam -- the heat of it) and the lye becomes salt; acid meeting sodium (tag:alkali) gives hydrogen and salt.

PACKAGE E: 5 -> 20, with the generic `-> air` rule above it cut 45 -> 25 to pay for it (same total eaten, about a third of it fuming). Bounded: every fume is a voxel acid ATE -- the gas is paid for in matter, it decays at 12 per-mille, and the acid spends itself on the dissolvable rule between.

-------- lye: caustic --------
Eats organic matter a tenth as fast as acid eats flesh, and is spent doing it (it weakens to water), so a spill scars the grass under it and stops. Reaches bodies through the inbound pass like acid. Neutralized by acid (acid's rules above).

-------- fairy dust enchants water and blood: NO PAIR RULE --------
The solute layer owns this (package B, docs/PLAN_solutes.md): fairy dust DISSOLVES into water or blood (solutes.json `fairy`), the mass spreads through the liquid, and a cell concentrated past the species' `converts` cMin BECOMES enchanted_water / enchanted_blood (sim_step.wgsl solTryConvert). A pinch in a lake disperses below cMin and enchants nothing; a handful in a basin enchants it. The two placeholder pair rules package A authored here (one grain turned the cell it touched) were removed when the layer landed.

-------- brine electrolysis: the chlor-alkali cell (package B) --------
Salt WATER touching a spark (tag:electric) splits: 2 NaCl + 2 H2O -> Cl2 + H2 + 2 NaOH. Both rules are gated on the DISSOLVED salt with the solute layer's concentration condition ("solute": "salt", "cMin": 24 -- brine, not a pinch; sim_step.wgsl solRuleAllows, the rule side array): fresh water under a spark does nothing. The first rule makes lye of the water and chlorine of the spark, the second hydrogen of the water and chlorine of the spark, so a shocked brine pool fumes both gases and turns caustic. Appended at the END of water's bucket (no earlier water rule's RNG stream moves). Simplification: the lye keeps the water's dissolved salt (lye is a salt solvent in solutes.json), so the salt is not consumed. A CPU evaluator with no solute (a body, the bench without its own solute model) must treat these as unmet -- MaterialDef::ruleFx[k].solute / RuleNeedsSolute.

======== PACKAGE E: THE CREATIVE EXPANSION (2026-09-27, docs/PLAN_alchemy_chemistry.md) ========
Forty-four new materials (materials.json, the rows after `spark`) and their chemistry, real and lore. Every rule below is APPENDED, so it is the last of its material's bucket and re-rolls nothing authored before it (rule index is part of the reaction RNG stream). They run in the WORLD and, through the same compiled table, on the ALCHEMY BENCH (game/flasksim_mats.h BuildBenchChemistry: a burner is a virtual tag:hot neighbour, Electrify a virtual spark, gases vent from the mouth into the world, and a rule's effect is a bench event by kind).

RECIPES, in one place (the notes below say why each number is what it is):
  gunpowder     saltpeter + charcoal -> black_mix; black_mix + sulfur -> gunpowder; heat or a spark -> EXPLODES (wet it and it is spoiled to charcoal)
  smoke bomb    saltpeter + sugar -> smoke_powder; heat -> smoke_charge, which pours thick_smoke and burns out to ash
  lime          chalk + heat -> quicklime; quicklime + water -> slaking_lime (HOT for a second: boils, ignites) -> slaked_lime; slaked_lime + choke_damp -> chalk
  thermite      rust + aluminium -> thermite; heat -> molten_iron (with a white glare), which cuts iron and steel and quenches to iron
  vitriol       acid + copper -> blue_vitriol (dissolves blue: the `vitriol` solute); blue_vitriol on iron -> copper + rust ('iron into copper')
  acids         acid + saltpeter -> aqua_fortis (parting acid: silver, copper, lead, iron -- never gold); aqua_fortis + salt -> aqua_regia (dissolves GOLD)
  quicksilver   quicksilver + sulfur -> cinnabar; cinnabar + heat -> quicksilver + fume; quicksilver + heat -> poisonous vapour
  fire          phosphorus lights itself in AIR (keep it under water); acid + aluminium -> hydrogen; acid + sugar -> charcoal (the carbon snake)
  spirits       sugar dissolves -> syrup; syrup + fungus (the yeast) -> spirits + choke_damp; spirits + acid -> ether; ether EVAPORATES to heavy ether_vapour, which EXPLODES near a flame
  frost         frost_salt + water -> ice (about three a grain); + lava -> stone; + steam -> snow; snuffs fire
  holy water    enchanted_water + salt -> holy_water; it SEARS rot (tag:infectious -> flesh_charred) and purifies ichor
  sun and moon  silver + water under the NIGHT sky -> moonwater; gold_dust + water under the NOON sky -> sunwater; each fades back under the other's sky
  the stone     sunwater + moonwater (the chemical wedding) -> philosophers_stone, rarely, with a flash; the stone on lead -> gold_dust, crumbling as it works
  light         luminous_spores sprout into glowcap on damp ground, at once in moonwater; heat pops a glowcap back to spores; spores dissolved -> glow_potion
  slime         fairy_dust + ichor -> slime; slime eats carrion (rotflesh, ichor) one for one; salt and heat kill it
  dragon        dragons_blood on skin -> dragonhide (Siegfried); heat -> it ERUPTS; water hisses it away

RULE 2, for all of it: every conversion is one-for-one or SPENDS its reagent (a catalyst -- silver, gold dust, the stone, frost salt -- carries its own spend rule at a fixed ratio), every gas decays, every hot transient decays, and every blast goes through the capped explode path. Nothing here grows from nothing, and nothing emits forever: the smoke charge is the only emitter and it burns out in ~2 s.

EFFECTS: `explode` is the world's and the bench's (gunpowder, ether vapour, dragon's blood). `flash` (thermite, phosphorus, the chemical wedding, a transmutation) is a burst of `glare` round the cell in the world (game/session.cpp ReactFxToBlasts, capped at 4 a tick, merged by radius) and a word at the bench.

IGNITION SCALING: a rule whose product is hot, or a hot neighbour acting on a FLAMMABLE self, is multiplied by combustion.spreadPct (29% as shipped). Every such rule below is authored knowing it (gunpowder's 1000 reads as ~290 per-mille a hot face).

-------- acid: its share of fume, and what it does to the new things --------
The organic fume rule is the other half of the rebalance at acid's first rules (organic 125 -> 85 + this 40). Then: saltpeter distils into aqua fortis (real: nitric acid was made from saltpeter and oil of vitriol), copper becomes blue vitriol, aluminium gives off hydrogen, sugar chars to carbon and steam (the carbon snake), chalk FIZZES off choke damp (CO2) and is neutralised to water, the caustic limes neutralise to salt and steam (lye keeps its own, earlier, rules), and lead pits very slowly. None of saltpeter, copper, aluminium, sugar, chalk or lead is tagged dissolvable, which is what lets these rules -- appended AFTER acid's generic dissolve -- be the ones that fire.

-------- holy water and slime, from package A's materials --------
Salt in enchanted water makes HOLY WATER (real root: holy water is blessed water with salt in it). A pair rule so it works in the world today; on the bench the `salt` solute's convert row (solutes.json) does it by concentration as well. Fairy dust in ICHOR quickens it into SLIME -- the ooze of a rotten thing given life.

-------- GUNPOWDER: saltpeter + charcoal + sulfur --------
Mixing is contact: two powders poured together meet at every grain boundary, and each rule turns BOTH grains into the mix (one-for-one, conserving). Saltpeter + charcoal is black_mix (sulfurless powder: it burns fast and fizzes, no bang); black_mix + sulfur is gunpowder. The mix rules are 120 per-mille, so a stirred flask turns in a second or two and a pile poured on a pile turns only where they touch.

Gunpowder + heat: selfBecomes fire and an EXPLODE effect, radius 3 power 130 (a grenade is 13/380; stone is hardness 90, and at 90 a bed of 162 grains set off 16 blasts and cut no crater at all). Authored 1000 and scaled by combustion.spreadPct (gunpowder is flammable and the neighbour is hot) to ~290 per-mille a hot face; a drifting flame at half of that (neighborChance -- a flame is how a fuse works). The blast's own aftermath lays fire in the crater, which lights the next grains: a pile goes off as a short string of bangs, bounded by the 4-a-tick cap, the merge radius and the powder itself. A spark lights it through spark's own `tag:flammable` rule. WET POWDER will not fire: water washes the saltpeter out and leaves charcoal.
Sulfur burns with a choking fume (real: sulfur dioxide) -- a share of its burn is noxious gas. Charcoal catches a little easier than wood (15 against 12) and smoulders as ember.

-------- SMOKE BOMB: saltpeter + sugar -> smoke_powder --------
Heat lights it into smoke_charge (authored 300, ~87 per-mille scaled), which is hot -- it lights the next grain and anything flammable, as a real smoke grenade does -- and EMITS thick_smoke into its open faces. Its decay is the FIRST rule in its bucket, so its lifetime (~66 ticks at 15 per-mille) is fixed whatever it emits, and a grain pours out ~25-30 cells of smoke and is ash: bounded, and never a standing emitter (the dew rule that pinned 250 chunks awake is the cautionary tale). thick_smoke hangs ~8 s.

-------- THE LIME CYCLE: chalk -> quicklime -> slaked lime -> chalk --------
Chalk over heat calcines to quicklime slowly (8 per-mille: a kiln, not a flash; not an ignition, so unscaled). Quicklime meeting anything wet SLAKES: it becomes slaking_lime -- tag:hot for about a second -- and the water it drank is steam. Being hot, slaking lime boils the water beside it and lights straw and wood through their own heat rules, which is the real hazard of wet quicklime; then it decays to slaked lime. Slaked lime drinking choke damp (carbon dioxide) sets back into chalk: lime mortar curing. Quicklime also hastens ROT to ash (the plague-pit trope -- in truth it slows decay, and this line is lore). Choke damp is heavy, puts fires out (tag:extinguisher, every douse rule already answers it) and fades (3 per-mille).

-------- THERMITE: rust + aluminium --------
Mixed by contact (one-for-one). Lit it becomes MOLTEN IRON. Hard to light: 60 authored, ~17 per-mille against lava or an ember after spreadPct, a drifting flame a sixteenth of that -- but molten iron lights the next grain at FIVE times the base (neighborChance), ~87 per-mille a face, so once it goes a pile burns through in seconds. Each grain that catches FLASHES (the `flash` effect: a burst of glare round it in the world, capped 4 a tick and merged by radius; a word at the bench). A spark lights it (its own rule).

Molten iron: burns organics like lava (60), sets sand to glass, QUENCHES to iron in water with a burst of steam, and CUTS iron and steel -- it hands its heat to the plate cell and freezes to iron itself, one for one, so the melt tunnels into a plate for as long as it stays molten and no longer (rule 2: there is never more molten iron than there was). It cools to iron on the inverted hot ramp molten salt uses, from the skin in, faster the less heat is round it.

-------- BLUE VITRIOL, QUICKSILVER, CINNABAR --------
Blue vitriol laid on iron gives COPPER and leaves the iron rust (Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu: the iron goes into solution and the copper plates out) -- the real reaction that convinced alchemists metals could be transmuted. Slow (10 per-mille).

Quicksilver takes up sulfur into cinnabar (60), and over heat gives off a poisonous vapour (noxious_gas, 15 -- unscaled: not fuel, not a hot product). Cinnabar roasted gives the quicksilver back (20) with a sulfurous fume (5).

-------- AQUA FORTIS and AQUA REGIA --------
Aqua fortis (nitric acid) is PARTING ACID: it eats silver, copper, lead and iron (each with a share of fume -- real nitric acid on copper boils off brown fumes) and flesh, and NEVER gold; that is how gold was assayed out of silver. Salt turns it to aqua regia (150). Aqua regia dissolves GOLD -- the solid gold (30 + a fume) and gold dust (50) -- and everything aqua fortis does short of silver (real: silver chloride skins over and stops it). Both are spent by what they dissolve (the dissolvable self-spend, 10) and neutralised by the caustics (lye, the limes) to salt and steam. On a body both eat like acid through the inbound pass; neither has a coat (the stain palette is full).

-------- PHOSPHORUS: lights itself in air --------
A DECAY rule gated on its AIR faces (scaleByNeighbors over `air`: no air face, no chance -- the ramp's count-0 gate), so a grain with an open face catches on its own (40 authored, ~12 per-mille scaled, up to twice that fully exposed: a pile in the open smokes for a few seconds and flares) and a grain under water, with no air beside it, NEVER does -- which is exactly why it is stored under water. Not a pair rule with neighbour `air`: the grid's pair loop skips air faces (sim_step.wgsl), so such a rule only ever fired on the bench. Each flare flashes (the glare burst). A burning neighbour lights it at the usual rate.

-------- SPIRITS and ETHER --------
Spirits burn readily (400 authored, ~116 scaled; a drifting flame a quarter). Spirits touching acid become ETHER (20; the acid is the catalyst and is not spent -- the spirits are). Ether is the most volatile thing here: every cell with an air face EVAPORATES (25 per-mille, a decay gated and scaled on its air faces -- the phosphorus rule's form) into ether_vapour, which is HEAVY (gas_heavy: it sinks and creeps, sim_step.wgsl stepHeavyGas) and near a flame or a spark CATCHES as ether_burning, a heavy flame that lasts ~2 s a cell and lights the vapour beside it (see ether_burning below -- it replaced a radius-2 blast, 2026-09-29). A vapour cloud burns through as a chain bounded by the vapour itself; left alone it disperses (5 per-mille).

ETHER BOILS OFF AS ~8 VAPOUR A VOXEL (owner, 2026-09-29: 'liquid ether should give off like 8 gas ether before it disappears'). Two rules with one ratio: the EMIT puts a vapour cell into an air neighbour and keeps the liquid (233 per-mille), and the decay after it turns the liquid itself into the last vapour (43). Both need an air face -- the emit only fires into air, the decay is gated on one (scaleByNeighbors, scaleMax 1: gated, NOT scaled, so the ratio holds whatever the face count). The emit is rolled first, so the decay fires with (1 - 0.233) x 0.043 = 0.033 a tick: 0.233 / 0.033 = ~7 emits, then the conversion = ~8 vapour per liquid voxel, and a surface voxel still lasts ~30 ticks (~1 s), what the old single 25..50-per-mille decay gave it. The vapour it makes is heavy and pools on the liquid, covering the air faces both rules need -- a puddle in a pit smothers its own boil-off until the vapour creeps away.

-------- ether_burning: the vapour ALIGHT (2026-09-29) --------
Replaces the radius-2 blast the vapour used to set off (owner: a lit voxel that burns for a couple of seconds is far more destructive than one that annihilates instantly). The ignition above is authored at 1000 and compiles at x spreadPct (~290 per-mille per hot face at 29%), so the flame front runs through a cloud in a handful of ticks, cell to cell -- ether_burning is tag:hot and lights the vapour beside it. Each lit cell then burns for ~2 s: the decays are burnDuration rules, 34 authored / burnDurationPct 200 = ~17 per-mille, a mean of ~60 ticks at 30 Hz. While it burns it throws `fire` up into any air above it, which is what reaches a ceiling or a canopy over the pool. Water puts it out.

-------- SUGAR and SYRUP --------
Sugar burns (30, scaled). It DISSOLVES into water as the `sugar` solute (solutes.json) and a saturated cell becomes syrup there -- a solute convert, on the bench and in package B's world layer; there is no pair rule for it. Syrup beside a FUNGUS (the yeast) ferments: most of it into spirits (6 per-mille), a little into choke damp (1). Slow on purpose: brewing takes a while.

-------- SLIME --------
Salt kills it (300: slime becomes water and the salt is used up -- the slug trope), heat boils it (150). It EATS CARRION: rotflesh and ichor it touches become slime (20 each), one for one, so a slime grows only by what it finds and never by itself (rule 2). On a zombie that is the rot being eaten off it.

-------- HOLY WATER --------
It SEARS THE ROT: anything tag:infectious (rotflesh -- a zombie's rot, a bitten wound going bad) becomes flesh_charred and the water hisses to steam (200). On a creature that is a BURN (flesh_charred is a burn stage, so it counts into the burnt fraction that caps health, DESIGN.md 'Blood is health, and burns cap it'): the undead are hurt where they are rotten, and a bitten living creature has the infection seared out at the price of a burn. Ichor it purifies back to water and is not spent by it (150). Boils like water.

-------- MOONWATER, SUNWATER, THE PHILOSOPHER'S STONE --------
SILVER (Luna) steeped in water under the open NIGHT sky makes moonwater (60); GOLD DUST (Sol) under the open NOON sky (minLight 160) makes sunwater (60). Both dusts are SPENT at 3 per-mille whatever the sky -- a pinch makes a handful and is gone, and by day (or indoors, or on the bench, which has no sky) it is simply wasted. The spend rule is also what keeps the chunk awake while the dust works: a light-gated rule never holds a chunk awake by itself (gotcha: light-gated rules never sleep), so without it a still pond would never be steeped at all. Each water fades back to plain water under the OTHER sky (2 per-mille, light-gated, so a still pond or a stoppered flask keeps it).

THE CHEMICAL WEDDING: sunwater meeting moonwater, at 4 per-mille, becomes one grain of the philosopher's stone (and the moonwater plain water), with a FLASH. The stone on LEAD makes gold dust (30, with a flash) and crumbles as it works (8), so a grain of stone is about four grains of gold -- a miracle, not a mine. Sunwater also sears rot, more gently than holy water (100, and it is spent), and thaws ice.

-------- LUMINOUS SPORES, GLOWCAP, THE POTION OF LIGHT --------
Spores in MOONWATER sprout at once (200, the moonwater spent to plain water); on damp ground slowly (dirt 3, mud and wet moss 5 per-mille: minutes, and the matched rule keeps only that chunk awake until they have). One spore, one glowcap. Heat POPS a glowcap back into spores (100, scaled as fuel) rather than burning it, one for one. Dissolved in water the spores are the `lumen` solute and a concentrated cell becomes glow_potion (solutes.json); the potion boils like water and otherwise only glows.

-------- DRAGON'S BLOOD --------
On SKIN it hardens the skin to dragonhide and is spent in a hiss of smoke (25) -- bathe in it and you come out scaled (the Nibelungenlied). Dragonhide has no tags at all, so fire, acid and rot have no rule for it; only blades and blasts, against hardness 120. Heat makes the blood ERUPT: it becomes fire with an explode effect (radius 3, power 60), authored 300 and scaled to ~87, a drifting flame a quarter of that. Water hisses it away (both to steam, 60); it melts ice and snow.

-------- FROST SALT --------
Endothermic: water it touches FREEZES (80), and the salt is spent (25), so a grain makes about three voxels of ice. It quenches lava to stone and molten iron to iron (300, spent), snuffs a flame to smoke (300, not spent -- a flame is not heat enough to use it up), and turns steam to snow (100). Every conversion is bounded by the salt or by what it touches; the ice it makes is ordinary ice and melts by ice's own rules.
-------- glare: the flash effect's light, gone in two or three ticks --------

-------- oil_burning: a POOL of oil alight (2026-09-30) --------
What oil becomes beside heat (oil's gated decay, above). ~10 s a cell: the two retire decays are burnDuration rules FIRST in the bucket, so the lifetime is fixed whatever the emits do. MEASURED, not derived: 13.4 authored / burnDurationPct 200 = 6.7 per-mille reads as a ~150-tick mean, but the `oil-fire` gate measures a lit cell burning TWICE that (half the authored 6.7 burnt 20.1 s), so the realised per-tick rate is half the compiled one here. Retune against the gate's `burn` number (oilFire.burnSecObserved), not the arithmetic. While it burns it throws fire up (the flames over the pool) and pours BLACK SMOKE out of its open faces, ~0.2 a tick -- ~60 cells over a surface cell's life, against the handful a burning plank gives off. Bounded (rule 2): emits only into air, and every cell retires. Water does not douse it (a grease fire floats and keeps burning); choke damp smothers it back to oil (which relights if the fire is still beside it), and rain puts it out slowly.
black_smoke fades a little slower than smoke (6 against 9 per-mille, ~5.5 s).

coolant (an android's bleed until 2026-10-03; nothing bleeds it now, materials.json) dries away like blood so a spill goes back to sleep (rule 2). DRYING: the alchemy bench never fires it inside a vessel. Appended: re-rolls no earlier rule.
